newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Police in Cyprus release two Turks held in probe.
newsitem.headline: Police in Cyprus release two Turks held in probe.

text.p: Police in Cyprus on Sunday released a Turk and a Turkish Cypriot held since March 9 in an ongoing espionage probe, citing insufficient evidence.
The two men were detained with another man, a mainland Turk, who is still in custody on suspicion of spying on Greek Cypriot military positions on the divided island.
"They were released today," a police spokesman said.

Police said they found maps and video tapes of sensitive military areas in the possession of Nejip Sari Cicekli, a mainland Turk who has been living in the southern coastal town of Limassol for more than 10 years.
The eastern Mediterranean island has been divided since 1974, when Turkish forces invaded in the wake of a Greek Cypriot coup engineered by the military ruling in Greece at the time.
Police have said Cicekli was working on behalf of Turkish intelligence for the past 18 months.
